Playbook.name: Windows — File or Directory Deletion Command - SOC Playbook

Metadata.Category: Defense Evasion / Indicator Removal - File Deletion

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A command to delete files/history ran - rundll32 InetCpl.cpl Clear (clear browser history), reg delete, or cmd/del of files. Triage question: is this anti-forensic evidence removal, or routine cleanup?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Deleting files/history removes forensic artifacts; done after other suspicious activity it is anti-forensics.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

Signal.Name: File deletion
Signal.Details: rundll32 InetCpl Clear, reg delete, cmd del.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the deletion is anti-forensic cleanup after activity or routine.

Step.name: What was deleted and by which parent
Step.Purpose: The deletion target and parent separate routine cleanup from evidence removal.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND process.command_line IS NOT NULL AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL cl = TO_LOWER(process.command_line) | WHERE (cl LIKE "*inetcpl.cpl,clear*") OR (process.name RLIKE "(?i)reg(.exe)?" AND cl LIKE "*delete*") OR (process.name RLIKE "(?i)cmd(.exe)?" AND (cl LIKE "*del *" OR cl LIKE "*rmdir*" OR cl LIKE "*erase *")) | KEEP @timestamp, process.name, process.parent.name, process.command_line, user.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: Clearing browser history via rundll32 InetCpl, or deleting logs/tool artifacts, right after suspicious activity = anti-forensics. Routine temp cleanup is benign. Correlate with what preceded it.

Step.name: Did suspicious activity precede the deletion
Step.Purpose: Deletion right after credential/execution activity is evidence removal.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code IN ("4688","4624","4672","7045") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | STATS c = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code) | LIMIT 5
Step.AnalystNotes: Privileged/execution activity before the deletion supports anti-forensics; a quiet host supports routine cleanup.

Node.Condition: Deletion of history/logs/tool artifacts following suspicious activity on the host.
Node.Result: True Positive (Anti-forensics - investigate the preceding activity)

Node.Condition: Routine temp/cache cleanup with no suspicious context.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-DELETE-DETAIL, INV-02-DELETE-PRECEDING to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Investigate what was deleted and what preceded it; reconstruct from SIEM; open IR if intrusion confirmed.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A cleanup tool deleting broadly by design.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
